newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma says more detainees released.
newsitem.headline: Burma says more detainees released.

text.p: The Burmese state media said on Friday that 25 more pro-democracy activists had been released, bringing to 188 the total number freed since hundreds were arrested in a crackdown on the democracy movement last week.

A total of 573 activists were originally detained by authorities, in a move to stop a meeting of opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy (NLD) party that had been set for September 27-29.
State-run media said on Friday the latest round of releases took place on Thursday.
The ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) had said it detained the NLD party members and supporters temporarily for questioning and would release them later.
Suu Kyi had disputed the total number arrested and said she believed the number held was closer to 800.
Meanwhile, police continued to bar access to Suu Kyi's residence on University Avenue to the public. Originally, police had said the checkpoints would be removed last Sunday.
Suu Kyi usually addresses the public on weekends from the gates of her residence, but with access still barred, it appeared unlikely that she would be able to make her regular speeches this weekend.
